headline: South Asia: Aramco skyscraper damaged as Houthis target Riyadh financial district
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Aramco skyscraper damaged as Houthis target Riyadh financial district.
- Western Russia: Russians strike emergency workers at attack site in Komyshuvakha, Zelenskyy responds.
- India: 'Trying To Obtain Nuclear Weapons': Israel Says 'Iran Mission' Not Complete.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: SIMMER DOWN - Tougher sanctions needed to curb parliamentary tensions, lecturer warns.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: SIMMER DOWN - Tougher sanctions needed to curb parliamentary tensions, lecturer warns.
With tensions in Jamaica’s Parliament escalating this week, a government lecturer is calling for tougher sanctions against lawmakers who breach parliamentary procedures, warning that failure to act could see the House of Representatives degenerate into a “brawl”.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: Privy Council shuts door on Dawkins Brown’s fight to regain accountant’s licence.
The United Kingdom-based Judicial Committee of the Privy Council has refused Dawkins Brown permission to appeal his removal from Jamaica’s Register of Public Accountants, bringing his latest attempt to overturn the disciplinary decision to an end. The refusal, handed down last month, means Brown has failed to secure a hearing before Jamaica’s highest appellate court in his battle against the Public Accountancy Board (PAB), which struck him off the professional register in March 2020 and ordered him to pay $1.6 million towards the costs of its disciplinary proceedings.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: Why achieving your goals can leave you feeling so empty.
THE CONVERSATION: When Anne Carson learned she had won the Nobel Prize in literature, she was in Iceland, where, according to the Swedish Academy, she was "listening to the wind". Carson didn't answer her phone right away, silencing it until her husband persuaded her to call back. Her verdict on the academy's choice: "I think you're all insane." Whatever she felt in the moment, there is an irony in Carson's Nobel win. The highest award in literature has gone to a writer who has spent her career exploring the emptiness of a desire fulfilled.
United States - bottom line: How Afghanistan War soul-searching led to renaming of Navy expeditionary command.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: How Afghanistan War soul-searching led to renaming of Navy expeditionary command.
The command's recent name change was years in the making after the end of the Afghanistan War, according to the head of Commander, Navy Expeditionary Forces.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russians strike emergency workers at attack site in Komyshuvakha, Zelenskyy responds.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 9 hours ago: Russians strike emergency workers at attack site in Komyshuvakha, Zelenskyy responds.
No emergency workers were injured, but rescue equipment was damaged. Zelenskyy said search operations continue after a Russian airstrike killed 55 people.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: Russia has attacked Ukraine with 115 missiles and over 3,000 drones this week, Zelenskyy reports – video.
Zelenskyy says Russia has also launched nearly 1,900 guided aerial bombs; the president has called for stronger sanctions against companies involved in missile production.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: One killed and three injured in Russian attack on Dnipro suburb – photos.
A drone strike destroyed a house in a residential area. Two women and a man received medical assistance at the scene and declined hospitalisation.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: People injured and houses damaged in Russian attack on Khmelnytskyi Oblast.
Firefighters extinguished a fire in Khmelnytskyi Oblast after Russian strikes damaged 12 homes and destroyed a house.
Southern Europe: no notable developments in the last 24 hours.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Ukraine: Russian strikes hit Kyiv region, damaging infrastructure.
- Africanews, 21 hours ago: Ukraine: Russian strikes hit Kyiv region, damaging infrastructure.
Russian strikes have damaged infrastructure in the Kyiv region and left a kindergarten in ruins in the Ukrainian capital. Firefighters battled a major blaze as Ukraine faced renewed attacks on its energy network.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Russian strikes on Ukraine leave hundreds of thousands without electricity.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, Politico Europe, 6 hours ago: Russian strikes on Ukraine leave hundreds of thousands without electricity.
About 850,000 people lose power after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk and Kharkiv.
- Jerusalem Post, The Hindu - International, 6 hours ago: ‘No good options’: Iran war caught between Trump's midterm troubles, Israel's election shake-up.
A broader offensive, continued pressure, negotiated compromise, or a limited strike are potential options, according to Raz Zimmt, director of the Iran and the Shiite Axis research program at INSS.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, The Hindu - International, Taipei Times, just now: Poland mourns six killed in attack as authorities launch ‘terrorism’ probe.
'Terrorism' investigation launched after government officials say suspect likely influenced by far-right ideology.
- Jerusalem Post, 2 hours ago: No to the war against the haredim, yes to Israel’s security - opinion.
Israel’s reservists are carrying an enormous burden, while sanctions have failed to deliver a breakthrough in haredi enlistment. A three-year legislative framework could replace confrontation.
South Africa: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Aramco skyscraper damaged as Houthis target Riyadh financial district.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, NDTV - Top Stories, South China Morning Post - China, 4 hours ago: Aramco skyscraper damaged as Houthis target Riyadh financial district.
An Aramco building in Riyadh was targeted in an “attempted attack”, the Saudi energy ministry said on Sunday, with eyewitnesses telling AFP the skyscraper sustained damage, after the Saudi-led coalition fighting Houthis said it had intercepted missiles launched by the group. Houthis claimed responsibility for the attack. Aramco facilities and infrastructure have been repeatedly struck by the rebels in Yemen in recent months, with tankers, refineries, storage areas and the company headquarters all targeted by the group.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 21 hours ago: Israeli president picks Netanyahu's rival Gadi Eisenkot to try to form government.
Israel’s president on Saturday chose Gadi Eisenkot, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s strongest rival, to try to form a new government following a deadlocked election that left neither man with a clear path to power. Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving leader, is fighting to stay in office after his religious-nationalist coalition lost its majority in an Oct 27 election but still emerged as the largest bloc in parliament. Eisenkot, a former military chief, has declined to join forces with Arab parties, with whose support he would have a majority of seats in parliament.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: KP plans to set up faceless ATCs, spend Rs70bn on CTD and police in a year as part of counterterrorism initiatives.
The administrative setup in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa plans to establish faceless anti-terrorism courts in the province as part of its initiatives to strengthen the fight against terrorism, according to a briefing by the officials televised on Sunday. KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi was also present at the briefing, where KP Secretary Home Amjad Ali Khan outlined several measures planned to step up the fight against terrorism and explained that witnesses in terrorism cases feared coming forward. “So, we have recently sent the amendment to set up faceless anti-terrorism courts.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: Broken record: Pakistan struggles with refugee influx; US supports Iran against the Soviet Union.
As Pakistan took its first few steps, the massive logistical task of accommodating millions of refugees in the midst of widespread communal violence was a major challenge for the state. The issues of Sept 8-14, 1947, documented these difficult times. In happier news, the Urdu Anjuman met for the first time in Karachi, while in a strange twist of history, the US came to Iran’s defence in the face of Soviet threats. The great migration The partition of the subcontinent had resulted in one of the largest — and bloodiest — mass migrations in human history.
India - bottom line: 'Trying To Obtain Nuclear Weapons': Israel Says 'Iran Mission' Not Complete.
- NDTV - Top Stories, The Hindu - International, 6 hours ago: 'Trying To Obtain Nuclear Weapons': Israel Says 'Iran Mission' Not Complete.
Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz renewed charges that Iran -- attacked twice since last year in major Israeli-US bombing campaigns -- is pursuing nuclear weapons, a claim that Tehran denies.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 7 hours ago: Russia targets Ukrainian rescue workers at site of Zaporizhzhia bombing that killed 55.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: Video: Jaipur cafe owner beaten after objecting to employee's friend's frequent visits.
A cafe owner named Mayank Gopalia was attacked by unidentified assailants in Jaipur on November 5. He was ambushed while walking home after closing his cafe, Oven The Bakery Cafe. The attackers repeatedly struck him with sticks, leaving him severely injured and unconscious. A preliminary investigation suggested threats from a friend of a female employee he had an altercation with earlier.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 13 hours ago: ‘Don’t talk to pups’: Drama unfolded at Faridabad police station hours before murder.
Monu Sharma allegedly shot Paramjeet Dhankar during a confrontation over a damaged gate in their parking area. Before the shooting, Sharma had threatened Dhankar at a police post, warning he would not leave him alive. The incident escalated when Sharma called Dhankar to discuss the car parking issue. Following the shooting, police teams collected evidence from the scene at the housing complex.
Asia - bottom line: India questions US ‘double standards’ as Pakistan secures F-16 upgrade deal.
- South China Morning Post - China, 11 hours ago: India questions US ‘double standards’ as Pakistan secures F-16 upgrade deal.
Washington’s decision to upgrade Pakistan’s F-16 fighter jets has drawn accusations of double standards from critics in India, who question why the United States is strengthening a nuclear-armed ally while waging war against Iran over its nuclear programme. China’s newest land-based intercontinental ballistic missile, the DF-61, has made its way into routine military training much faster than earlier ICBMs, according to state broadcaster CCTV. That raises the question of whether the People’s Liberation Army is becoming more efficient at integrating new strategic missiles into its nuclear forces. - South China Morning Post - China, 4 hours ago: Indonesian firefighting helicopter crash in Borneo kills 1.
A crew member of a helicopter battling Indonesian wildfires was killed on Sunday when the aircraft crashed into a river as it scooped up water for an airborne drop, a local disaster agency said. The crash in Borneo Island’s South Kalimantan province was the second in days involving a firefighting aircraft, after a military helicopter plunged into the waters off Borneo on Wednesday, killing three people. Two Australian pilots survived Sunday’s crash and were “safe”, Berton Panjaitan, a spokesman...
- South China Morning Post - China, 6 hours ago: Defects at Hong Kong MTR station ‘unimaginable’, engineers and lawmakers say.
Mistakes that left about 30 columns defective at a Hong Kong railway station under construction were “unimaginable”, lawmakers and engineers said on Sunday, adding that the repairs were expected to be straightforward and unlikely to delay the project. The MTR Corporation was also urged to set up a reporting mechanism that would allow frontline workers to flag problems during construction. The comments came a day after the Buildings Department revealed that about 30 columns at the MTR’s Tung...

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Two Australians rescued after helicopter crashes into Borneo river.
- ABC News Australia, 9 hours ago: Two Australians rescued after helicopter crashes into Borneo river.
Video shows the helicopter collecting water for water-bombing operations in Indonesia's South Kalimantan province before it loses control and crashes into the river.
- ABC News Australia, 16 hours ago: Palestinians return to destroyed West Bank homes after IDF siege.
Wael al-Jabaa's home was demolished by the IDF after two Israeli soldiers were shot dead. He didn't know until afterwards that his son was one of the gunmen.

Reflecting on Julia Gillard's now-iconic speech, Tony Abbott says he thought it was "pretty over the top" and saw it mostly as an example of political theatre.
